r.description: approximate route of Charles II's escape

r.name: Wychavon Way
r.description: A route from Holt Fleet on the River Severn to Winchcombe in the Cotswolds.

r.name: cycle route Cradley Heath to Old Hill
Northwick - Ladywood Cycle Leisure Route
r.description: Circular route starting at the Pump House Environment Centre and covering a mixture of quiet lanes and residential streets.The route is 10.5 miles with a short cut that reduces it to 6.5 miles.

r.name: Staffordshire Way (Cannock Chase South)
r.description: Staffordshire Way, part Cannock Chase - south

r.name: Wychavon Way (old)
r.description: A route from Holt Fleet on the River Severn to Winchcombe in the Cotswolds.

r.name: Royal Hunters Walks - Saunders Park to Park Gate Link
Rea Valley Route
r.description: NCN 5 section of Rea Valley Route

r.name: Doulton Trail (Saltwells LNR)
r.description: Walking trail around a bluebell-covered Ancient Woodland and nationally important heritage urban nature reserve. Includes one long and steep flight of stairs but generally good surfaced paths and gentle gradients.

r.name: Murray Gray Trail (Saltwells LNR)
r.description: This trail leaves the cover of trees and leads to the summit of Netherton Hill where the resident herd of Murray Gray Cattle may be seen. Includes 1 stile, 2 road crossings, several ascents/descents, including one steep, and potentially muddy paths.

r.name: GeoTrail (Saltwells LNR)
r.description: Geologic trail around the historic national nature reserve across 2 periods of earth's history. Initially the oldest rocks show change from seabeds to desert. The second series shows huge swampy forests with 45m+ trees that created the coal seams.

r.name: Bromsgrove-Redditch Cycle Route 24
r.description: From Bromsgrove Station to Redditch Station. Follows mostly open countryside on road.

r.name: Dudley Port Circular
r.description: Follow The Gower Branch, then turn right back onto The Old Main Line. For a more challenging route, continue along The New Main Line and cross at Bromford Junction. Take the ramp access to The Old Main Line and double back, crossing Blakeley Hall Bridge.

r.name: Rowley Hills Geology Trail
r.description: A self-guided circular walk around the summit and the northern slope of Rowley Hills, taking in 15 points of interest. Not suitable for disabled/buggies due to rough ground, steep slopes and steps.

r.name: Lye Town History Trail
r.description: Discover the hidden history and architecture of Lye High Street along this clockwise circular trail. Duration: 54 mins

r.name: Brierley Hill Architectural Heritage Trail
r.description: Walking tour around the historic buildings of Brierley Hill dating back to the 1600s

r.name: Brierley Hill Geological Heritage Trail
r.description: This geotrail explores the stones and landscape features that tell stories of ‘deep time’ linked to the very formation of the planet itself, and of this local hill on which this town stands.

r.name: William Shenstone & The Leasowes Historical Trail
r.description: A walk around The Leasowes highlighting examples of the landscaping of poet William Shenstone, who lived here and developed it from grazing farms to one of the first natural landscape gardens of England in the 1700s

r.name: The Leasowes Blue Walking Trail
r.description: Blue trail 2.1km – 45 minutes. Moderate difficulty with some undulating ground and one short climb. Gravelled paths lead you around the woodland valleys & watercourses.

r.name: The Leasowes Red Walking Trail
r.description: Red trail 3.3km – 1 hour 15 minutes. Moderate difficulty with some undulating ground and one short climb. Gravelled paths lead you around the woodland valleys & watercourses.

r.name: Halesowen Architectural Heritage Trail
r.description: Explore the history of Halesowen through its historical buildings. From the early C13th, Halesowen was a thriving market town due to Halesowen Abbey, becoming a local centre for woollen cloth weaving and as a regional market centre for corn.

r.name: Stourbridge Canal & Glass Quarter Heritage Trail
r.description: Discover the glass-making history and heritage of Stourbridge, over the last 400 years

r.name: Black Country Canals: The Dudley & Stourbridge Ring
r.description: 'Circuit' of Canals surrounding Dudley & Stourbridge. Follow the fascinating network of junctions and branches through scenery varying from industrial warehouses to suprisingly secluded rural lengths.

r.name: The Crystal Canal Walk
r.description: A canalside walk through Britain's heart of glass. Stourbridge became world-famous for making iron and glass. To discover why, follow this trail along Town Arm of the Stourbridge Canal to Britain’s most complete working ‘glass cone’.

r.name: Bourn Brook Walkway
r.description: Walking route along the Bourn Brook from near to the University of Birmingham to Woodgate Valley

r.name: Stourbridge Town Arm Walk
r.description: A waterside walk, following the route of The Stourbridge Town Arm for approximately one mile from The Stourbridge Bonded Warehouse to Wordsley Junction. Distance: 3 miles/4.8 km(approx) Duration: 60 mins(approx)

r.name: Delph Walk
r.description: This linear walk takes you from the modern Merry Hill, through changing landscapes and down the rural tranquillity of the historic lock flight and back. Distance: 1.5 miles/2.4 km(approx) Duration: 30 mins(approx)

r.name: Stourbridge Circular (Leys Junction to Delph Locks)
r.description: Follow Stourbridge Canal down scenic locks, then takeStourbridge Town Arm to Bonded Warehouse, follow NCR54 through suburbia, rejoinin the canal at Black Delph and go left at Leys Junction to return to Dell Sports Centre. Route includes low footbridge!

r.name: Walk Rowley Regis Heritage Trail
r.description: Heritage trail around Rowley Regis, once ‘Ruh Leah,’ saw settlements at Blackheath, Cradley Heath, Old Hill & Tividale due to fertile land & rich resources. Rowley was known for nail, chain, nut & bolt making, pottery, coal mining & quarries.

r.name: Leasowes & Coombeswood Countryside Walk
r.description: This walk, east of Halesowen, takes you through the Leasowes and into the Coombeswood area of Dudley’s green belt. Length: 4km (2.5m) Duration: 2 hours

r.name: Centenary Trail, Kinver Edge
r.description: Medium difficulty, some short steep slopes and uneven paths. Explore heath and woods, sweeping views, restored Rock Houses, and the remains of Nanny's Rock and Vale's Rock. Cyclists permitted.

r.name: Blakeshall Trail, Kinver Edge
r.description: Medium difficulty through the woodland and conifer plantation with some steep slopes passing the unique Vale's Rock Houses. https://www.accessable.co.uk/national-trust/kinver-edge-and-the-rock-houses-national-trust

r.name: Heathland Trail, Kinver Edge
r.description: Easy stroll with gentle slopes. Passing through heathland habitat, to breath-taking views from along the edge and the Hill Fort.

r.name: Kinver Edge Village Trail, Kinver Edge
r.description: A gentle stroll from Kinver Edge to Kinver Village High Street, with some steep slopes, some walking on the road, and through countryside and quiet village streets, leading to the quaint shops and cafes of Kinver.

r.name: Woodland Trail, Kinver Edge
r.description: Medium difficulty, some steep slopes and steps. Discover restored Holy Austin Rock Houses, enjoy woodland and views from the Hill Fort.

r.name: The Buzzard Trail, Clent Hills
r.description: The Buzzard Trail takes you past Clent’s Four Stones, through woodland and offers fantastic views across the region. Please be aware that, although this is the easiest of our new trails, both the footpaths and terrain on this walk can be uneven.

r.name: The Badger Trail, Clent Hills
r.description: The hardest of our new walks, the Badger Trail takes you around the periphery of Clent and Walton Hills. Please be aware this is a challenging trail; the terrain on this walk can be uneven and this walk includes very steep inclines and steps.

r.name: The Rabbit Trail, Clent Hills
r.description: Take in some of Clent Hills best-loved features and viewpoints on the Rabbit Trail. Please be aware the footpaths and terrain is uneven and this walk includes steep inclines and steps.

r.name: The Butterfly Trail, Clent Hills
r.description: Explore both Clent and Walton Hill on the Butterfly Trail. Please be aware this is an intermediate trail, both the footpaths and terrain on this walk can be uneven and this walk includes steep inclines and steps.

r.name: Short Walk, Clent Hills
r.description: A wide all-ability path, with compacted gravel and little gradient, suitable for pushchairs and most wheelchairs. The circular route returns via a steeper and slightly more uneven woodland trail.

r.name: BCN Walks- Titford Canal
r.description: The Titford Canal walk starts below the M5 at Oldbury Locks Junction, climbs Oldbury Locks, and finishes at Titford Pools. Built 1773-4, the pools are the BCN's highest point at 511ft and connect to the navigable Causeway Green and Portway branches.
